[ASSISTANT_SAID] Cities typically have laws and regulations in place that govern the buying and selling of properties, which apply regardless of whether microfilm technology is used.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Property transactions may be overseen by government agencies or officials to ensure compliance with laws and to prevent fraud or unethical practices.  
[USER] User raised a concern about the accuracy and potential tampering of microfilm records.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Cities usually have measures in place to ensure the accuracy and security of microfilm records, including regular auditing, access control, backup systems, and encryption.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Regular audits are conducted by city officials to ensure microfilm records are accurate and up-to-date.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Access to microfilm records is typically restricted to authorized personnel to prevent unauthorized changes or tampering.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Backup systems may include physical copies, digital backups, or both to safeguard microfilm records.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Encryption and other security measures may be used to protect the security of microfilm records.
